children: Enterprise software company Salesforce Inc. (CRM, Financials) is coming into Dreamforce with lots of emphasis already on its AI business. The company is behind one of the world's most frequently used customer management platforms.

The company has completed its acquisition of Fin, a workflow analytics startup that helps businesses discover where work is getting stuck and how employees are using software. It's in line with Salesforce's desire for increased automation. But Wall Street isn't waiting around for a second acquisition.
Ahead of Dreamforce and Salesforce's analyst day Sept. 15-17, RBC Capital analyst Rishi Jaluria maintained a hold rating and $250 price target.

The main focus will be on Salesforce's AI model layer built with Anthropic, called Claudeforce. Investors will want to know about pricing, features and, most crucially, whether customers are using it.
Agentforce is already at $1.5 billion in annual recurring income. With Data 360, that value climbs to $3.9 billion. The figures are promising. They also make the next update more complicated.
Salesforce has been warning investors for years AI could be a significantly greater part of its growth story. That's where Dreamforce comes in to prove that this is happening, in real time.

For investors, the next few days are less about fresh product and more about proof that. If adoption continues to grow, Salesforce will be able to make a stronger argument that its AI approach is becoming a business, not just a pitch.

title: Salesforce Is Heading Into Dreamforce With a Lot to Prove
